key_insight: A basin-scale tracer flux balance links thermohaline circulation tipping to competing advective and dissipative transport, unifying box-model and continuous-ocean dynamics.
engineering_relevance: Tracking tracer gradients and transport efficiency could improve ocean-model diagnostics of tipping risk beyond monitoring overturning strength alone.
method: Derive surface-flux balances from tracer conservation using large-scale gradients and transport efficiency.
Evaluate transport contributions in a three-dimensional ocean-basin model.
Apply a simple circulation closure to connect weak- and strong-flow regimes to box-model bifurcations.
evidence_signal: The basin-model results indicate that nonlinear salinity advection dominates the collapse threshold, while linear dissipation dominates recovery; tracer transport scales approximately quadratically with weak circulation and linearly with strong circulation.
watch_item: Evidence here comes from an ocean-basin model, not observational validation, and tipping-point forecasting closures are deferred to Part II.
paper_title: Basin-Scale Nonlinear Dynamics of Thermohaline Ocean Circulation. Part I: Theory
